overview: This file documents concern over the deteriorated condition of Japan’s postwar railway system and the subsequent effort to improve freight transportation under the Allied Occupation. It begins with consulting engineer Howard G. Hill’s August 1947 warning that wartime overuse, deferred maintenance, and shortages of materials and equipment threatened railway safety and economic recovery, followed by State Department correspondence tracing his report after the death of George Atcheson Jr. The later documents comprise a June 1948 despatch from Tokyo and an enclosed SCAP press release setting a national freight target of 424 million tons and describing requirements for freight cars, repairs, fuel, rubber, scheduling, and communications. The enclosure also contains unrelated occupation-era notices concerning the prosecution of Japanese naval personnel for POW beheadings and the repatriation of Koreans apprehended while entering Japan illegally.

subfiles.title: Hill letter warning of the condition of Japanese railways
subfiles.to: George C. Marshall, Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Hill asks the Secretary of State to forward to George Atcheson Jr. his report on the dangerous condition and material needs of Japan’s railways.
subfiles.summary: Hill warns of Japan's railway crisis from wartime overuse and deferred maintenance, enclosing an inspection report, following talks with Atcheson.

subfiles.title: Bishop acknowledgment of Hill’s railway report
subfiles.about: Bishop acknowledges Hill’s letter and explains that the report was forwarded to the U.S. Political Adviser in Japan following Atcheson’s fatal accident.
subfiles.summary: Bishop confirms Hill's report was sent to Tokyo's Political Adviser after Atcheson's fatal accident, expressing the thanks Atcheson would have given.

subfiles.title: Howard G. Hill business card
subfiles.about: The card supplies Hill’s Washington address, telephone number, and professional identification as a consulting railway engineer.
subfiles.summary: Howard G. Hill's business card lists his Washington address, phone number, and consulting-railway-engineering specialty.

subfiles.title: Handwritten request for prompt handling
subfiles.about: An internal note asks that Hill’s matter be handled and that a reply be obtained that day if possible.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten note asks the recipient to take charge and reply promptly to Hill's continued inquiries.

subfiles.title: Reams memorandum requesting confirmation from Tokyo
subfiles.from: R. B. Reams, Office of the Secretary
subfiles.about: Reams asks Far Eastern Affairs to determine whether Hill’s report reached Tokyo and to write to him.
subfiles.summary: Reams asks Penfield to confirm whether Hill's railway report reached Tokyo, as previously promised, and send Hill a response.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Hill’s attempted meeting with Department officials
subfiles.about: The memorandum asks whether Humelsine will meet Hill or arrange a meeting with someone in the Division of Northeast Asian Affairs.
subfiles.summary: Hill, seeking Carter, requested a meeting with Humelsine; Northeast Asian Affairs staff couldn't identify who handled his report after Bishop left, leaving Hill unhappy.

subfiles.title: Allison invitation to discuss Hill’s railway report
subfiles.about: Allison confirms that Hill’s report was sent to the U.S. Political Adviser in Japan and offers to meet with him.
subfiles.summary: Allison learns of Hill's effort to discuss his report with Bishop, confirms it was forwarded to Tokyo's Political Adviser, and invites Hill to meet him anytime.

subfiles.title: Copy of Hill’s letter to Secretary Marshall
subfiles.to: George C. Marshall, Secretary of State
subfiles.about: This retained copy repeats Hill’s request that his report on Japan’s railway crisis be forwarded to George Atcheson Jr.
subfiles.summary: Hill writes Secretary Marshall describing dangerous Japanese railway conditions from wartime overuse and shortages, urging U.S. material aid and forwarding his report to Atcheson.

subfiles.title: Copy of Bishop’s acknowledgment to Hill
subfiles.about: This file copy records the forwarding of Hill’s report to the U.S. Political Adviser in Japan after Atcheson’s accident.
subfiles.summary: Bishop acknowledges Hill's letter, explaining the report was held for Atcheson's arrival, then forwarded to Tokyo's Political Adviser after Atcheson's fatal accident.

subfiles.title: Tokyo despatch on Japan’s freight requirements
subfiles.from: Acting U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards a SCAP press release estimating Japan’s fiscal 1948–49 freight requirements and the improvements needed to meet them.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo despatch reports Japan must move 424 million tons of freight for recovery, needing 4,500 new freight cars, repairs to 60,000 cars, amid gasoline and rubber shortages.

subfiles.title: SCAP press release on freight, war-crimes charges, and Korean entrants
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Far East Command, Public Information Office
subfiles.about: The enclosure presents SCAP’s transportation program for Japan together with notices on a Yokohama war-crimes proceeding and the return of Korean unauthorized entrants.
subfiles.summary: Besson details Japan's 1948 freight-movement targets (424 million tons, 130 million by rail) amid fuel shortages; the release also reports war-crimes charges for beheading U.S. airmen on Sulawesi and 519 Koreans repatriated that week.

interest: Shows a stalled 1947 railway-crisis warning entangled with Atcheson's death, and 1948 freight-reconstruction targets for Japan.
